summary: This work proposes superconducting singlet-triplet (SST) qubits—hybrid devices based on parallel-aligned double quantum dots in Josephson junctions—that combine spin-based quantum computing with circuit QED while avoiding the need for spin-orbit interaction. The SST qubits achieve all-to-all connectivity using only $N$ flux lines for $N$ qubits and exhibit linear protection against charge and flux noise.
motivation: Andreev spin qubits have shown strong experimental progress in hybrid superconductor-semiconductor devices, but they require spin-orbit coupling to access the spin degree of freedom, limiting their material platforms. A platform that retains the advantages of Andreev qubits—long-range coupling and circuit QED compatibility—while working in materials lacking intrinsic spin-orbit coupling would enable broader implementation of hybrid superconducting spin qubits.
method: Two quantum dots in parallel within a Josephson junction are coupled via crossed Andreev processes, with the interaction strength $E_\mathrm{CA} = 2\Gamma^2/|\epsilon|$ (where $\Gamma = \rho_F \pi t^2$) controlled by the superconducting phase $\phi$ across the junction. A magnetic field gradient creates a Zeeman energy difference $\delta h$ between dots. The resulting qubit Hamiltonian $H_\mathrm{DDJJ}' = \frac{E_\mathrm{CA}}{2}[1+\cos(\phi)](\tau^x-1) + \frac{\delta h}{2}\tau^z$ is derived from second-order perturbation theory in the large-$\mathcal{U}$ limit.
result: Single-qubit gates are realized by setting $\phi=0$ (X set point) or $\phi=\pi$ (OFF set point) with arbitrary rotations achieved via flux pulses. Two-qubit gates with $\tau_j^x \tau_k^x$ interaction arise at $\phi_j=\phi_k=\pi/2$ (INT set point), enabling controlled-Z gates with duration $T = \pi\hbar E_J/(E_\mathrm{CA}^j E_\mathrm{CA}^k)$ when $\delta h \ll E_\mathrm{CA}^j E_\mathrm{CA}^k/E_J$. The idle OFF state is protected to linear order against flux noise ($\cos(\phi)$ expansion suppresses first-order fluctuations) and charge noise variations affecting tunnel couplings (quadratic protection from $\delta\Gamma$ corrections).
